summary: npm package ships only a fake Cloudflare Turnstile HTML lure as main entry
details: The package contains no JavaScript entry point, no lifecycle scripts, and no dependencies. Its only shipped file is an HTML page titled 'Just a moment...' that mimics a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge and embeds a large obfuscator.io-style inline script (hex-encoded string array, `_0xXXXX` identifiers). The package.json `main` field points at this HTML file, so `require()` or `import` of the package from an installer resolves to a non-executable asset and performs no action at install, import, or require time. The artifact's shape is consistent with using the npm registry (and downstream CDNs such as unpkg/jsDelivr) to host a browser-side phishing / ClickFix-style lure page targeting end users who load the HTML via a CDN URL, rather than developers who install the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
